test_BlockBackstopClosesRoundWhenChainSt.details: And the block count still closes it if the chain stalls and time      stops advancing — the backstop must not be defeated by a frozen clock.

test_EnterAutoAdvancesAndRefundsAbandone.details: The headline case: a round expires with one player in it. Normally      that stake sits stranded until someone presses "settle". Here the      NEXT player to enter flushes it automatically — the solo entrant is      refunded in full, inside that same transaction, and the new entrant      lands in the fresh round. Nobody is ever locked out.

test_EnterDoesNotAdvanceWhileRoundIsLive.details: Auto-advance must not fire while the round is genuinely still open,      or every entry would burn a round. This keeps the optimisation from      being a foot-gun.

test_GameRecoversAfterEmptyRound().details: The round after an empty one must still be playable, proving the      game recovers rather than merely avoiding the revert.

test_LateEntryCannotJoinAtStalePrice().details: The core anti-time-travel property. Entering late must never be      settled at the closed round's original entry price.

test_LoserDoesNotTieWithBreakevenOnFlatC.details: The bug this guards: PnL must be signed, or a losing player ties      with a breakeven player and can win the pot on a flat curve.

test_LoserRanksBelowBreakeven().details: Guards the regression where an unsigned magnitude let losers tie      with breakeven players.

test_RejectsEntryAfterCloseBlock().details: Regression guard: a late entrant must never land in the round that      already closed, at its stale entry price. enter() now auto-advances      instead of reverting, so the property to assert is that the entrant      ends up in the NEW round and the old round's entry price is frozen.

test_RoundClosesOnWallClockAlone().details: The wall-clock deadline must close the round on its own, without      waiting for the block backstop. enter() now auto-advances past the      expired round rather than reverting, so the deadline's effect shows      up as a brand new round with a fresh entry price.

test_SecondsRemainingTracksWallClock().details: Regression: the countdown used to be derived from block count with      an assumed 100ms/block. This chain runs ~180ms/block, so the      number under-reported and the UI looked frozen. It must now be real      wall-clock seconds, and must hit 0 exactly at the deadline.

test_SettleWithZeroEntrantsDoesNotBrick(.details: Regression: a round that expires with ZERO entrants used to      divide by zero (`amount / n2`) and revert, which permanently      bricked settle() — and since settle() is the only path that opens      the next round, the whole game would be unplayable after the first      empty round. Found by playing against a live anvil node.
